title: Iron Gate

source.title: US task force to cut off Iran's transport of advanced weapons: What we know
source.note: published 11-08 14:06 UTC; the 11-08 sweep matched it on 'iran' alone. Read in full on 11-09 via the cloud fetch (complete, 28 body paragraphs) as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. An explainer — the roster's cuttable form for this source; four outside readers (Mulroy, Zweiri, Khouri, Kent) carry fourteen of the twenty-eight paragraphs. Cut 11-09 from the 11-08 sweep as the LI corner's full-text row on the live object (the war's conduct, the gate) — newest first after the NYT rows, which are β only

object.label: H6 — the gate (PG01, proposed 10-15: US control of the Strait of Hormuz), read from the LI corner outside the US horizon five days after the vote: the blockade of Iran's ports extended to its seven land borders and the Caspian Sea — 'Task Force Iron Gate' (CENTCOM, Saturday 11-07; Tampa; about twenty people; advanced weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials, illicit revenue). The gate was physical for three weeks (the Strait, the mines, the blockade), legal for one (the Act, the licence, the letters — aj 11-06); on this page it goes to land. Around it the force: a reader's target list if the holder escalates (economic and infrastructure, not military — Mulroy); the WSJ's report that Cooper and Hegseth are pressing the holder to renew attacks; the IRGC's underground complexes to build under bombardment. Against it the gate's reach disputed from three sides — a former official in the holder's own camp ('policy by CONOP' — the military subverting the office's talks), Tehran ('a play on words'; the two-week collapse that did not come) and two regional readers (no US presence on the Caspian; eleven percent; thousands of years of trade). The pump, the vote and the price are not on the page; the Strait is there only as the blockade at sea the land gate 'reinforces'

zAxis.pos: the gate holds and the war closes on US terms — supply and revenue cut off, the talks the office is holding bear fruit
zAxis.neg: it does not — the land routes and the Caspian stay open, the task force is a step toward renewed strikes, the war widens (Russia) rather than ends

object.gear: the war itself (the war tracker, event marks); nothing on the pump, the vote or the dollar; the Strait by reference

transformNote: the holder's promise is not on the page and neither is he, except as the man who may 'escalate' (¶9). What the page does to the object is move the gate: the deal's gate turned legal on 11-06, and here the war's gate turns to land — a blockade reinforced by a coordination body against seven borders and a sea the US cannot reach. The force runs under it as on every Al Jazeera page since 10-27: renewed war 'looms' (¶1), the target list (¶10), the pressure on the holder from his own commander (¶24). The vote enters once, obliquely — the office 'negotiates' while CENTCOM 'invites escalation' (Kent) — the ticket's split seen from outside the US horizon as a split between the office and the command

log.what: daily cut over the 11-08 sweep (no 11-09 sweep on GitHub at 07:00 PT; the newest date in the index used, said so). Twenty-eight body paragraphs read in full via the cloud fetch; fifteen scored (the hed, the author's seven, the readers' seven), none constitutive — the holder is not on the page and the IRGC is stationed with the publication (the Baghaei precedent). Object declared on H6, the gate, moved to land; the force and the ticket's split carried as the record beneath. My calls: Kent stationed with the publication rather than RP; the IRGC Dia-scored rather than @O; every line on the 'war' tracker for the tracked Lumens (the page has no pump, vote or dollar line), whose readings are event marks with sigma 0 — the proximity the formula gives is 1 − |z + 1|, so the figure measures how far each voice's z sits from 'the war' and nothing else; reported, not ruled

split.note: one corner, five voices beside the hed. The author: 22 → 18 → 14 → 20 → 16 → 10 — fluid throughout, the record carried flat; the hedge (¶28) the page's floor. The readers: Mulroy 24 → 26 (the strategy named, the targets listed); Zweiri 38 → 28 (the confrontation with Russia high, the sizing low); Khouri 52 → 30 (the verdict on method high, the trade routes low); Kent 48; the IRGC 36. Rule 5 across the page: the page is most denominated when a reader judges Washington's competence or intent ('off the cuff', 'inviting escalation', 'confrontation with Russia') and most fluid when it counts — seven borders, twenty people, eleven percent, a fraction. Nothing on the page is about the price; the gate is read as force and as geography

lines.quote: 'cut off Iran's transport of advanced weapons'; 'as fears of an escalation grow'
lines.note: THE DOOR (hed + dek) — the gate named in CENTCOM's own verb; the force in the dek
lines.zWhy: a gate announced as fears of escalation grow is a war widening, not closing

lines.quote: Washington widens the squeeze on Tehran's supply lines 'as renewed war looms'; Task Force Iron Gate for the land routes and the Caspian; CENTCOM, Saturday: stop advanced weapons moving by ground
lines.note: the record dated — the gate's announcement and its reach; 'renewed war looms' the author's clause
lines.zWhy: a squeeze widened under a looming war reads the war as continuing

lines.quote: the same day, the IRGC's plan for underground complexes to keep missiles and drones in production under bombardment; construction near missile bases (BBC, satellite imagery); Tehran's claim the strikes failed to reach the underground sites
lines.note: the other side's record on the same day — production hardened for a longer war
lines.zWhy: a factory built to run under bombardment expects the bombardment

lines.quote: where weapons enter, how to cut them off, how Iran moves its energy; a coordination body for an 'economic strangulation strategy' — maritime covered, now the ground
lines.note: the mechanism named by a former official: the gate as strangulation, the sea done, the land next — two paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: a strategy of strangulation is a war fought on, by other means

lines.quote: the port blockade extended to the land borders and the Caspian; reportedly 20 civilian and military personnel; seven neighbours — Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Pakistan, Turkiye, Turkmenistan; Tampa; weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials, illicit revenue; Cooper: it 'reinforces' the blockade at sea
lines.note: THE GATE SIZED — three paragraphs folded; the Strait on the page only here, as the sea blockade the land gate reinforces
lines.zWhy: a blockade extended is a blockade still needed

lines.quote: if the holder escalates, a 'series of targets' is likely — economic and infrastructure, not Epic Fury's military ones — to cut the regime's ability to fight and fund itself
lines.note: THE FORCE — the target list, from a reader who held the Middle East desk; the war's next phase described before it is ordered
lines.zWhy: a target list drawn for the next phase reads the war as not ending

lines.quote: 'just a play on words'; the US cannot collapse the economy this way; Washington said Iran would collapse 'within two weeks' and it did not
lines.note: the other party's counter — a boast with a dated falsifier inside it (the two weeks that passed) — three paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: a party counting the weeks its collapse did not come reads the gate as not holding

lines.quote: CENTCOM did not name Russia; US media: drone components and explosives to Iran via the Caspian; Russian technology toward advanced supersonic cruise missiles
lines.note: the Russian route — the register's object (fox 11-06 'Russia secretly bolstered', uncut) on the LI page; two paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: a supply route named is a war supplied

lines.quote: Russia-linked imports 'a real concern'; the task force could 'cause a confrontation with Russia'
lines.note: THE WIDER WAR — the reader's reading of where the gate leads; two paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: a gate that risks Russia widens the war it was built to end

lines.quote: the US 'doesn't quite know' how to handle Iran, acts 'off the cuff'; the approach has achieved little
lines.note: the reader's verdict on method — the right domain, the wrong plane (competence, not the gate); the page's highest line
lines.zWhy: an approach that has achieved little has not closed the war

lines.quote: thousands of years of trade; contacts across the region, especially Asia; blockades cannot control Russians, Chinese, Emiratis; materials bought from the US or Europe and routed through Asian companies
lines.note: THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE — the gate's porosity, four paragraphs folded; the record of how the materials move
lines.zWhy: a gate on a trade of thousands of years is a gate with a thousand side doors

lines.quote: CENTCOM 'inviting escalation' while the vice president negotiates; 'policy by CONOP' — the military subverting the White House without defying the president
lines.note: THE SPLIT, SEEN FROM OUTSIDE — a former aide from the holder's camp names the gate as the command's move against the office's talks; the one line that touches the vote's instrument
lines.zWhy: a command inviting escalation against its own office's talks is a war the house has not agreed to end

lines.quote: the WSJ: Cooper, with Hegseth, pressing the holder to renew attacks on Iran
lines.note: THE PRESSURE — the force dated and named; later sighting of the split (fox 11-08: Hegseth and Netanyahu for renewed action) from the LI corner
lines.zWhy: a commander pressing for renewed attacks reads the war as resuming

lines.quote: largely symbolic — no US military presence on the Caspian; no access unless Azerbaijan or Armenia cooperate, which they will not; ground troops unlikely; the Caspian 'just 11 percent' of Iran's economy
lines.note: THE GATE SIZED SMALL — the reader's counter: a gate announced on a sea the US cannot reach; three paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: a symbolic gate neither closes the war nor widens it

lines.quote: Al Jazeera could not verify the 11 percent; the Soufan Center: the Caspian a fraction of Iran's overall maritime trade
lines.note: THE HEDGE — the publication's own, and the page's floor
lines.zWhy: a figure unverified reads neither way
